rows.title: Texas’ front-line workers in the pandemic are predominantly women and people of color, analysis finds
rows.standfirst: Sixty-two percent of front-line workers in the 11 Texas cities with the the largest populations of front-line workers are women, compared with 48% of all workers there, the analysis shows.

rows.title: Analysis: You didn’t think a pandemic could stop highway planning in Texas, did you?
rows.standfirst: All eyes in Texas are on the coronavirus and the state government’s response to it. But some of the biggest state agencies are still doing what they always do, like building highways and debating oil and gas regulations.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Texas State University System says it’ll resume on-campus classes in the fall
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas halted evictions, giving renters some relief. But what happens when the moratorium ends?
rows.standfirst: Experts and advocates say renters — hit particularly hard by the economic downturn — face a financial cliff if more monetary aid doesn’t arrive before moratoriums lift.

rows.title: T-Squared: The Texas Tribune Festival is going virtual
rows.standfirst: With no certain end to the coronavirus pandemic in sight, the show must go online. We’re excited! The new on-sale date for #TribFest20 tickets is June 1.

rows.title: Texas sales tax revenues fall by 9.3% in April
rows.standfirst: For the past several weeks, the comptroller has been referring to the state of the economy as a recession. The latest sales tax figures give the first glimpse of how much the economic downturn will hurt the state budget.

rows.title: Watch: Lawrence Wright knew the U.S. wasn’t ready for a pandemic. He talks to Evan Smith about why he tried to warn us anyway.
rows.standfirst: Smith talks with Wright, a best-selling author, about his new novel, “The End of October,” in the premiere episode of Paramount Conversations.

rows.title: “I do not want to die in here”: Letters from the Harris County Jail
rows.standfirst: A series of letters from detainees in one of America’s largest jails reveals the mounting dread and uncertainty as the coronavirus spreads inside the 7,500-inmate facility.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Sylvia Garcia of Texas predicts cities and local governments could be facing bankruptcy
rows.standfirst: Garcia said the country could be heading toward the next Great Depression.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott said museums can reopen — but there will be no tours of the state Capitol or Governor’s Mansion
rows.standfirst: The Texas historic landmarks previously offered frequent guided tours to the public. But there are no plans to open the Capitol or the Governor’s Mansion despite the governor’s order allowing museums to reopen.

rows.title: At a Texas mall reopening, some antsy shoppers wore homemade masks while others called coronavirus a farce
rows.standfirst: Friday was the first day that shopping malls — along with restaurants, retail outlets and movie theaters — were allowed to reopen in Texas. Under an order from Gov. Greg Abbott, stores can open their doors, but they must limit occupancy to no more than 25% of capacity.

rows.title: A prominent Texas man’s network of hotels got millions in taxpayer loans, irking smaller businesses and some lawmakers
rows.standfirst: Monty Bennett’s Dallas-based hotel network applied for $126 million from the government’s Paycheck Protection Program and has received $76 million, according to data compiled by The Washington Post.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Dallas-based hotel group to return $76 million in disaster loans meant for small businesses
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: She tried to get her at-risk brother out of a nursing home. Now he has COVID-19.
rows.standfirst: Listen to Karen Jones’ story in this weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: UT-Arlington selects provost to serve as interim president, puts long-term search on hold
rows.standfirst: Lim has been serving as administrator in charge since Karbhari’s resignation, and the UT System chancellor said in an email to the campus community that he has “been impressed by [Lim’s] leadership.”

rows.title: Feds send coronavirus strike force to Amarillo in response to outbreaks in meatpacking plants
rows.standfirst: Potter County has roughly four times the infection rate of Harris and Dallas counties.

rows.title: Dallas-based hotel group to return $76 million in disaster loans meant for small businesses
rows.standfirst: The network of companies — Ashford Hospitality Trust, Ashford Inc., and Braemar Hotels & Resorts — are run by prominent Texas GOP donor Monty Bennett.

rows.title: Tourism in a world with COVID-19
rows.standfirst: A Texas A&M tourism expert and an epidemiologist explain how both tourists and the tourism industry can manage during the crisis.

rows.title: Analysis: If reopening the economy is risky, who’s getting protection?
rows.standfirst: Top officials say it’s safe to reopen at least some of the economy, but they’re also pushing for “blanket immunity” for businesses, should anything go wrong. That leaves some people out.

rows.title: 70% of Texas prisoners tested have the coronavirus. Experts say it’s time for more testing and fewer inmates.
rows.standfirst: Some of the nation’s biggest COVID-19 outbreaks have been in prisons and jails, and they can quickly spread to surrounding communities. Are Texas prisons doing enough to protect inmates, staff and the public?

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Carnival to launch cruises from Galveston in August; oil regulator calls idea to cut production “dead”
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Pete Sessions incurs legal bills — and opponent’s criticism — in campaign to return to Congress
rows.standfirst: The former Dallas congressman has spent over $80,000 on legal fees since launching his campaign to replace retiring U.S. Rep. Bill Flores, R-Bryan.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Vicente Gonzalez suffers broken back, ordered to bed rest at least four weeks
rows.standfirst: Gonzalez’s office said he took a 12-foot fall at his home in McAllen.

rows.title: “Between 0 and 100%”: Texas schools weigh the odds of students returning this fall
rows.standfirst: It’s way too early to know how COVID-19 cases will trend over the next few months, but school leaders are trying to draw up preliminary plans for bringing students back to classrooms.

rows.title: “We need to find a way to protect health care workers”
rows.standfirst: A leading Texas A&M scientist and Chancellor John Sharp discuss a clinical trial aimed at keeping frontline medical professionals safe from worst effects of COVID-19.

rows.title: Health care workers are living in treehouses, RVs and hotels to protect their families from coronavirus
rows.standfirst: To avoid accidentally sickening medically fragile children or elderly parents with the new coronavirus, some health care workers are aggressively disinfecting their clothes and homes or trying to isolate themselves. The efforts can take a mental toll.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott’s press conference on Texas coronavirus updates
rows.standfirst: Among the governor’s announcements: Hair salons can reopen Friday, and gyms will be allowed to open May 18.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Dallas-based Gold’s Gym files for bankruptcy
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas agency won’t cut oil production despite cratering prices
rows.standfirst: Two global crises have brought unusual attention to Texas oil regulators, who decided against taking action some producers wanted. One regulator said, “Politics win, Texans lose.”

rows.title: 7 Wonders from the University of Arizona
rows.standfirst: Seven things that most exemplify the university’s purpose, values and spirit.

rows.title: In confirmation hearing for intelligence director, U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe promises he “won’t shade the intelligence”
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump has nominated the congressman from Texas to oversee the nation’s 17 intelligence agencies.

rows.title: GOP lawmakers got illegal haircuts while calling on Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to reopen salons
rows.standfirst: State Reps. Briscoe Cain and Steve Toth said there’s no reason to continue banning businesses from operating as long as they follow CDC guidelines. Such restrictions, the two said, are hurting the Texas economy.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott to allow Texas hair salons and pools to reopen Friday and gyms to open May 18
rows.standfirst: The governor had initially eyed May 18 as the next date to announce further business reopenings, but he faced growing pressure in recent days from some in his own party to move more quickly.

rows.title: Texas outlines guidelines to allow socially distant graduations to resume
rows.standfirst: School districts can keep their ceremonies virtual, celebrate seniors while they drive in a procession, knit pictures of individual seniors into a graduation video or host a socially distanced outdoor ceremony, said Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath.

rows.title: Abbott sending “surge team” to look at spiraling coronavirus rates near Texas meatpacking plants
rows.standfirst: As Gov. Greg Abbott continues lifting restrictions on Texas businesses and activities, coronavirus infection rates are exploding in Panhandle communities near meatpacking plants.

rows.title: Dallas salon owner who refused to close sentenced to seven days in jail, ordered to pay fines
rows.standfirst: Salon a la Mode owner Shelley Luther reopened Thursday even though the state had required nonessential businesses to remain closed.

rows.title: Analysis: Reopening Texas as hot spots multiply
rows.standfirst: State officials are gradually allowing the reopening of businesses and organizations that were closed to limit the spread of the coronavirus. Meanwhile, hot spots continue to flare in Texas — signs the virus is still raging.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Dan Patrick says economy can be fully reopened in “not too distant future”
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Rent assistance programs in Texas’ largest cities are running dry, but advocates say statewide relief is unlikely
rows.standfirst: Dallas, San Antonio and Austin recently implemented housing relief programs, and Houston will consider one this week. But local officials and advocates agree they aren’t enough to see Texans through the pandemic.

rows.title: “We need herd immunity”: U.S. Rep. Chip Roy of Texas says Americans can’t wait for a vaccine to return to normalcy
rows.standfirst: The firebrand Austin conservative spoke with The Texas Tribune’s Evan Smith about reopening the economy, voting in person and how he practices social distancing.

rows.title: Texas DACA recipients working on pandemic’s front lines await Supreme Court ruling
rows.standfirst: More than 4,000 DACA recipients work in health care in Texas, including many in hospitals. A pending U.S. Supreme Court ruling will decide whether they can continue that work — and stay in the country.

rows.title: Top Texas officials denounce Dallas salon owner’s jail sentence for defying orders to close
rows.standfirst: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton said the seven-day jail sentence was excessive. Paxton called for her immediate release.

rows.title: TribCast: The governor’s quicker-than-expected move to further reopen Texas
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Emma and Ross about the governor’s move to reopen more businesses in Texas more quickly than expected and the implications of those reopenings.

rows.title: Texas hair salons, barbershops and other beauty businesses can reopen Friday. Here are the rules they have to follow.
rows.standfirst: Limited services, face coverings and smaller occupancies are among the new rules businesses will follow if they open this Friday.

rows.title: Texas A&M researchers hope tuberculosis vaccine might prevent coronavirus deaths
rows.standfirst: Health care workers are being recruited for trials to test whether a decades-old TB vaccine might help people fight off the coronavirus. It’s not a cure, but it could be a crucial treatment.

rows.title: Trump order to paint border wall black could drive up cost $500 million or more
rows.standfirst: The president’s determination to have the border wall coated in black has fluctuated during the past several years. He has insisted that the dark color will enhance the wall’s forbidding appearance and leave the steel too hot to touch during summer months.

rows.title: Texans could soon have to start looking for work to keep unemployment benefits if reopening continues
rows.standfirst: The Texas Workforce Commission’s executive director told lawmakers that it plans to reinstate work-search requirements once stores and restaurants are allowed open to 50% capacity.

rows.title: “There’s no sense in risking it”: As Texas eases restrictions, a family keeps its social distance
rows.standfirst: The governor is allowing more businesses to reopen, and Texans are weighing the risks of returning to normalcy. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: 247,179 more Texans filed for unemployment, but their jobs might not be waiting for them when they return
rows.standfirst: The Texas Workforce Commission relaxed guidelines so high-risk workers and people without child care can refuse work and still receive benefits. But that doesn’t protect workers from being fired in the meantime.

rows.title: Dallas salon owner released from county jail after defying orders by reopening early
rows.standfirst: The order followed Gov. Greg Abbott’s announcement that he was eliminating jail time for Texans who violate stay at home orders.

rows.title: How gun control advocates plan to make Texas a top political priority in 2020
rows.standfirst: One group, Everytown for Gun Safety, has already committed $8 million to the state this election cycle and is now naming three hires, including two seasoned Democratic operatives, to help see the plan through.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Seven Corpus Christi beef plant employees test positive
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas A&M is looking at Saturday and late-night options to reduce class sizes and comply with social distancing
rows.standfirst: Chancellor John Sharp offered some ideas about what the fall semester could look like, but the system won’t have a finalized reopening strategy until at least the end of May.

rows.title: President Donald Trump applauds Gov. Greg Abbott’s handling of Texas reopening during White House visit
rows.standfirst: During the visit, Trump also inquired about Dallas salon owner Shelley Luther, who was freed from jail Thursday after being sentenced to seven days for violating a court order to close.

rows.title: Analysis: Splitting hairs in Texas, for politics and profit
rows.standfirst: The governor and other top Texas officials love promoting the rule of law, but they also love good politics. The civil disobedience of a Dallas beautician forced them to choose a favorite — and maybe hurry changes in pandemic policy.

rows.title: Coronavirus restrictions alter funeral plans, leaving some Texans to grieve alone
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott clarified this week that in-person funerals can be held if attendees stay 6 feet apart. But restrictions still have some postponing memorials until after the pandemic ends. “If you can’t hug anyone or shake their hand, what’s the point of having anyone physically attend?” one mourner said.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Austin extends stay-at-home orders to end of May
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Language barriers, absence of bank loans leave Latino small-business owners struggling
rows.standfirst: Before the pandemic, mom-and-pop stores at the Latino-oriented mall La Gran Plaza, in Fort Worth, saw crowds of thousands every day. Now, tenants are worried about evictions and not making ends meet.

rows.title: Business has reopened in Texas, but the economy won’t be back anytime soon, experts say
rows.standfirst: The Texas energy sector has helped insulate the state’s economy during national downturns. This time, experts say the industry could hold the economy back.

rows.title: Texas passes grim threshold, marking more than 1,000 COVID-19 fatalities
rows.standfirst: Texas seems to have fewer to mourn than some of the hardest-hit states. But experts say the official state death toll is likely an undercount.

rows.title: They just want someone to talk to: This mental health hotline is helping Texans navigate the pandemic
rows.standfirst: The Harris Center, a health authority in the Houston area, and the Texas Health and Human Services Commission — which had seen a 500% jump in traffic to its webpages on mental health and substance abuse resources — joined forces and provided the service to callers statewide March 31.

rows.title: As coronavirus shutdowns sink city budgets, Dallas furloughs almost 500 employees
rows.standfirst: Experts and local leaders have warned that the next fiscal year will be a historically hard one for cities.

rows.title: “I’m over it. I need a haircut.” Eager but nervous Texans venture back into busy salons and barbershops
rows.standfirst: Barbers reported being booked through the day due to pent-up demand related to the coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Dallas salon owner jailed after reopening wants to donate to Laredo beauticians arrested for working
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: He’s used to oil booms and busts. But this pandemic has destroyed his livelihood.
rows.standfirst: Odessa native Erik Mancha says this latest downturn in crude prices is unlike any other, largely because of the coronavirus pandemic. Listen to his account in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: Analysis: Reopening just a little bit isn’t really a big boon for the economy
rows.standfirst: Reopening Texas businesses in a contained way gives the appearance of thawing out a frozen economy while keeping crowds at bay. That might make people feel better, but it’s no way to supercharge an economy.

rows.title: Texas has billions in its rainy day fund. But legislators say they won’t use it until January.
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers widely agree that the Legislature will tap into the Economic Stabilization Fund next session. But under the weight of a crippled economy, many Texans want relief now.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: San Antonio expands free testing to asymptomatic residents; state to test all nursing home residents
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: COVID-19 cases at a Texas immigration detention center soared. Now, town leaders want answers.
rows.standfirst: Coronavirus infections continue to rise at migrant detention facilities in towns with limited resources. Some local governments want details on what’s being done to safeguard the public.

rows.title: Texas’ rules for mail-in voting won’t work during pandemic, a new lawsuit argues
rows.standfirst: In their suit, a group of Texas voters and civic organizations claim that four Texas absentee voting rules are unconstitutional during a public health crisis.

rows.title: Texas doubles early voting period for July primary runoff elections
rows.standfirst: Early voting for the July 14 runoffs will begin June 29, instead of July 6, under a proclamation issued Monday by Gov. Greg Abbott.

rows.title: “Every day for two weeks, I would cry a little”: Coronavirus takes a toll on clients and mental health professionals
rows.standfirst: Mental health counselors are seeing more demand for their help during the pandemic, and they’re feeling the weight of it, too.

rows.title: Analysis: The coronavirus hits Texans of color harder. You can see it in public opinion polling.
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus disproportionately affects people of color. And judging by what voters said in the last University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll, it’s evident that Texans of color express greater concern about it.

rows.title: Photos of a state in crisis: Deserted highways, swamped food banks and health care workers at risk
rows.standfirst: COVID-19 has changed the world in ways few imagined possible. As the virus spread across the globe and found its way to Texas, Tribune journalists and photojournalists have been there every step of the way, documenting the changes the new coronavirus has brought into all our lives.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Optional tests to help assess what public school students learned remotely
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: As her party railed against attempts to expand mail-in voting, a Texas GOP congressional candidate gave a “green light”
rows.standfirst: Kathaleen Wall, a Republican activist and donor in a runoff for a battleground U.S. House seat, has said the secretary of state expanded who is eligible to vote by mail. The secretary of state’s office says that’s not true.

rows.title: From 9/11 to COVID-19: Chief Nim Kidd answers the call
rows.standfirst: As Texas tries to recover from the effects of COVID-19, the head of the Texas Division of Emergency Management highlighted successes and challenges during a TV interview.

rows.title: Texas Railroad Commissioner Christi Craddick says recovering from oil and gas downturn “is going to be painful”
rows.standfirst: Craddick told The Texas Tribune in a live interview that a global price war and the coronavirus pandemic will continue hampering the state’s economy and budget.

rows.title: Complaint filed over Texas AG Ken Paxton’s tactics to limit mail-in voting
rows.standfirst: In a series of tweets and a public statement, Paxton said eligibility for absentee voting has not been expanded. But a state judge’s order says otherwise.

rows.title: Texas prisons to begin widespread coronavirus testing for inmates with self-administered tests
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Criminal Justice said it will begin having prisoners test themselves with a newly approved test. So far, less than 2% of state prisoners have been tested for the virus. More than 1,700 have been infected, and 30 have died.

rows.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton warns Austin, San Antonio, Dallas to loosen coronavirus restrictions
rows.standfirst: Paxton’s office said that there could be litigation if cities do not pull back coronavirus restrictions related to masks, sheltering in place and religious services.

rows.title: Texas’ age limit for mail-in ballots discriminates against Latinos, LULAC argues in new lawsuit
rows.standfirst: The civil rights group is raising questions of constitutionality and violations of the federal Voting Rights Act because the pool of voters eligible to vote by mail based on age is predominantly white.

rows.title: Race to replace U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe gathers steam as Republican activists set date to pick his likely successor
rows.standfirst: The Heath Republican is on track to be confirmed as the director of national intelligence, which would create a vacancy in his solidly red district.

rows.title: Analysis: In Abbott’s hands, executive orders look like suggestions
rows.standfirst: Even as Gov. Greg Abbott is loosening his pandemic restrictions on people and businesses, he is buckling to opponents who protest that he’s moving too slowly. He’s undermining his own authority — and enforcement of the rest of his rules.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: State reports highest one-day COVID-19 tests totals
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Coronavirus tests are supposed to be free. Some Texans are still being saddled with large bills.
rows.standfirst: Congress directed most insurance companies to cover test costs for insured patients in March, and has promised to reimburse providers for testing those who are uninsured. But experts say there are gaps in the protection that can leave patients surprised with bills.

rows.title: Wonder makes us map the universe.
rows.standfirst: Where did we come from? That’s a question Professor Chris Walker is searching the galaxy to answer, aided by University of Arizona facilities and expert personnel. In 2017, NASA selected the professor of astronomy in the university’s Steward Observatory as the principal investigator to help map the Milky Way.

rows.title: Cascade of endorsements animates Texas’ Democratic U.S. Senate runoff, which coronavirus has upended
rows.standfirst: A steady stream of endorsements has been illuminating some of the battle lines between MJ Hegar and Royce West as they vie to take on U.S. Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas.

rows.title: Texas bar owners say they’re going broke and are desperate for Abbott to lay out a reopening plan
rows.standfirst: Last month, the governor said he hoped to reopen bars “on or no later than mid-May.” He has since walked back the timeline for when bars can open their doors to customers, saying he needs more input from doctors.

rows.title: TribCast: The “don’t do as I say” coronavirus edition
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Ross, Emma and Matthew about the governor’s move to pull back on the enforcement of his executive orders related to the coronavirus pandemic and a GOP congressional hopeful’s misleading messaging on voting by mail.

rows.title: Texas meatpacking plant reverses course, will allow state to test workers
rows.standfirst: State health officials say the JBS Beef plant rejected its efforts to test all employees. The company switched gears Wednesday afternoon after the Tribune reported on the lack of testing at a plant tied to a rapidly growing cluster of coronavirus cases.

rows.title: Six candidates, including two well-known Democrats, file in special Texas Senate election to replace Kirk Watson
rows.standfirst: State Rep. Eddie Rodriguez and former Travis County Judge Sarah Eckhardt, both Democrats, are among those vying for the seat. So is former Austin City Council member Don Zimmerman, a Republican.

rows.title: Texas attorney general asks state Supreme Court to step into fight over voting by mail
rows.standfirst: Ken Paxton, a Republican, wants the state’s highest civil court to tell five counties — all under Democratic control — to follow his interpretation that fear of contracting the coronavirus isn’t a legally valid reason for voters to request absentee ballots.

rows.title: How Lina Hidalgo is navigating coronavirus and conservative backlash in Texas’ biggest county
rows.standfirst: Harris County has seen new cases plateau under the county judge. But her orders designed to slow the spread of the new coronavirus have generated outrage among some conservatives.

rows.title: Dallas food pantry worker gets a boost during the pandemic: a promotion
rows.standfirst: Mother’s Day brought tough decisions on whether to get together with family, and some took the risk while others spent the day apart. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: State reports largest daily increases in cases and deaths
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas is spending $45 million on new coronavirus tests that prisoners are administering to themselves
rows.standfirst: The state purchased 300,000 oral swab tests from a months-old California company. So far, only highly-infected prisons are using them for mass testing.

rows.title: Wonder makes us create our own stories.
rows.standfirst: If you’ve ever been moved by music, a play or a painting, then you know art’s transformative power. It’s something that Brad Richter, director of outreach for the University of Arizona College of Fine Arts and co-founder of the music education organization Lead Guitar, explores through a program he helped develop, Arizona Art in Schools, known as AZAiS.

rows.title: Former U.S. Rep. Pete Gallego named sole finalist for Sul Ross State University presidency
rows.standfirst: If confirmed in June, Gallego will be Sul Ross’ 13th president and the first alumnus to lead the school.

rows.title: Texas appeals court allows expansion of voting by mail during ongoing legal fight
rows.standfirst: The appeals court ruled against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who argued that a lower court ruling expanding who can qualify for an absentee ballot during the coronavirus pandemic should have no effect while he appeals it.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott is limiting enforcement of COVID-19 orders, but many cities already took a lax approach
rows.standfirst: Texas cities and counties have dramatically different interpretations of the state’s COVID-19 emergency orders. Complaint data from a dozen cities shows that disparate approaches to enforcement, particularly among businesses, have been incredibly common.

rows.title: Eviction proceedings and debt collections can resume this month, Texas Supreme Court orders
rows.standfirst: The state’s highest civil court initially paused eviction proceedings and debt collections during the coronavirus pandemic. Those moratoriums are being lifted after more than 1.9 million Texans filed for unemployment.

rows.title: Analysis: The path to emergency powers in Texas might run through the courts
rows.standfirst: State and local governments are at odds over what should and should not be allowed during a pandemic — a debate over health, economics and civil liberties. The old sparring partners have increasingly appealed to a referee: the courts.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says bring back sports and let fans in the stadiums
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: How a Dallas salon owner changed Texas’ reopening debate
rows.standfirst: After Shelley Luther was jailed for opening her salon in blatant defiance of emergency orders, top Texas Republicans in all three branches of government scrambled to ensure her release.

rows.title: Trump administration waives environmental safeguards to fast-track 69 miles of border fence construction
rows.standfirst: The White House said in February its goal was to build 450 additional miles of barrier by the end of 2020. The 69 miles would be in addition to a 52-mile project also underway in Webb County.

rows.title: As Texas reopens, coronavirus cases are increasing while testing misses benchmarks
rows.standfirst: Texas has seen a modest but steady increase in the growth of new coronavirus cases in the two weeks since some businesses reopened at 25% capacity. Gov. Greg Abbott sees hope in other metrics.

rows.title: Thousands of Texas nursing home residents have tested positive for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Among the 311 nursing homes with positive cases, there have been 3,011 residents infected. At assisted living facilities, nearly 400 residents have tested positive. At least 585 residents from both kinds of facilities have died.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court puts expansion of voting by mail on hold
rows.standfirst: The state Supreme Court’s order comes one day after a state appeals court had allowed the expansion to stand while a legal case was appealed.

rows.title: As Texas reopens for business, this San Antonio teen is scared about the risks of working as a restaurant hostess
rows.standfirst: In the weekend edition of The Brief podcast, listen to the 17-year-old describe the backlash she says she faced from customers when enforcing the governor’s social distancing guidelines.

rows.title: More than 700 new cases of coronavirus reported after testing at meatpacking plants in Amarillo region
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott says the cases were detected by targeted testing at meatpacking plants.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Gov. Greg Abbott says cities and counties shouldn’t raise property taxes
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: With COVID-19 cases rising, El Paso officials ask governor to exclude them from next phase of reopening
rows.standfirst: As state officials and some Texas cities tangle over local COVID-19 restrictions, El Paso officials say their area isn’t ready for the next phase of reopening. They want Gov. Greg Abbott to give them an exemption.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas tiptoes down the road to normal
rows.standfirst: As some pandemic doors are slowly opened, others are getting kicked in. Either way, individual choices are quickly replacing the weeks of government instructions about what and what not to do.

rows.title: “All of the party was over”: How the last oil bust changed Texas
rows.standfirst: A plunge in oil prices in the 1980s had ramifications across the state — even without landing at the same time as a pandemic and economic crisis.

rows.title: Child care centers, bars and sporting events scheduled for Texas’ next phase of reopening
rows.standfirst: Child care opens immediately, bars can open Friday and sports will be allowed to return at the end of the month, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott announced Monday.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Gyms, manufacturing facilities and offices open Monday
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Wonder makes us refuse to sit on the sidelines.
rows.standfirst: What can our bodies accomplish? A lot, if you ask Jen Poist. Each day, the University of Arizona women’s wheelchair basketball head coach heads to campus at 6:30 a.m. for two-hour basketball practice.

rows.title: Here’s what we know about Texas’ economic reopening, and what might be coming next
rows.standfirst: On Monday, gyms were allowed to reopen in Texas. What’s next for Texas’ reopening plan?

rows.title: Texas is testing everyone in nursing homes for coronavirus, but not state-run homes for people with disabilities
rows.standfirst: The facilities are still only testing residents and patients who are symptomatic or were potentially exposed to the virus, despite concerns raised by employees and family members about outbreaks.

rows.title: The Trump administration is rushing deportations of migrant children during coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Their father was missing. Their mother was miles away in Houston. Two sisters, ages 8 and 11, were survivors of sexual assault and at risk of deportation. With the nation focused on COVID-19, the U.S. government is rushing the deportations of migrant children.

rows.title: Opening up child care, camps helps working parents, but risks remain
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott’s decision to reopen child care centers and youth camps takes pressure off parents, but safety guidelines may be unaffordable for some providers.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says Texas ranks high in coronavirus recoveries, but many large states don’t report that figure
rows.standfirst: Texas’ recovery total is not a tally of the patients no longer experiencing symptoms, but rather an estimate based on a string of assumptions about the virus’ longevity.

rows.title: Texas schools can hold summer classes, but students can’t be required to attend in person
rows.standfirst: Daily temperature checks and supervised hand-washing are some of the safety rules for schools that decide to hold in-person classes this summer, under new guidance from the Texas Education Agency.

rows.title: Texas had plans to replace its outdated unemployment system. The coronavirus pandemic hit first.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Workforce Commission had finally lined up enough federal money to move the system — built in the 1990s — to the cloud. But before that happened, nearly 2 million suddenly unemployed Texans overwhelmed the old system.

rows.title: Renters prepare for tough choices as eviction proceedings resume in Texas
rows.standfirst: Unemployment has disproportionately affected renters since the crisis began. Advocates fear displacement and an increase in homelessness.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Medical experts say voting in person “certain” to spread infections
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: “It’s a bizarre time to be job searching”: College graduates looking for first jobs face catastrophic economic conditions
rows.standfirst: As 2020 college graduates prepare to enter the workforce, they are having to contend with a historic economic recession. Experts say those who do get jobs in the recession may accept lower wages and salaries than they’d have otherwise settled for.

rows.title: Senate committee advances nomination of U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe for director of national intelligence
rows.standfirst: The Texas representative’s nomination will go to the full Senate after receiving approval from the Senate Intelligence Committee.

rows.title: Texas scaling back child care subsidies for essential workers, low-income parents
rows.standfirst: A child care subsidy program for essential workers will stop taking applications after Wednesday, and on June 1, low-income parents will stop getting an extra subsidy they have been receiving to help during the pandemic.

rows.title: Dancing is discouraged: Bars, sports and child care centers can open if they follow these rules
rows.standfirst: Among the businesses reopening are day and overnight youth camps, professional sports without spectators and massage services.

rows.title: Federal judge says all Texas voters can apply to vote by mail during pandemic
rows.standfirst: District Judge Fred Biery granted a preliminary injunction that allows all registered voters to apply to vote by mail during the coronavirus pandemic after finding the state’s existing election rules violate the Equal Protection Clause.

rows.title: Budget cuts at UT-Austin will likely bring furloughs and layoffs, campus leaders say
rows.standfirst: The university is gearing up for a second wave of cuts brought upon by the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Trump administration announces extension of border-restricted travel
rows.standfirst: One of the policies quickly returns undocumented immigrants apprehended between ports of entry without allowing them to apply for asylum.

rows.title: Analysis: In spite of it all, a Texas government that’s running full-steam ahead
rows.standfirst: The pandemic has devastated the Texas economy. The state comptroller says that will mean billions of dollars less than expected for the current budget. But state agencies haven’t received any orders to cut their spending.

rows.title: Search the Government Salaries Explorer
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune’s database of compensation for Texas state employees has been revamped. It includes detailed data for all of the 113 agencies in state government and every position at each of those agencies.

rows.title: T-Squared: Introducing our new salaries explorer
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune is excited to launch a new and revamped version of our Government Salaries Explorer.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Texans still able to refuse work and receive unemployment benefits if they lack child care
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: She walked out of jail into a pandemic. Now she can’t find the help she needs to get back on her feet.
rows.standfirst: Many reentry services offered to those leaving incarceration — like help with housing and employment — have moved online or been halted since the new coronavirus hit the state.

rows.title: Texas school districts raise hands for shares of $1.29 billion federal infusion
rows.standfirst: Most of the money is expected to go directly to local districts to help vulnerable students during the coronavirus pandemic. But advocates are trying to steer some into controversial policies like expanding virtual schools.

rows.title: Watch: Texas Senate candidate Sarah Eckhardt discusses her campaign and how it’s evolved in response to the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: We sat down for a live virtual event with Eckhardt to discuss her campaign to succeed former state Sen. Kirk Watson and get her take on how the coronavirus pandemic has reshaped her campaign.

rows.title: Former Travis County Judge Sarah Eckhardt says Abbott’s actions to reopen Texas are divisive, scary and confusing
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s recent decisions to reopen the economy despite rising infection rates signal that something has “spooked” the governor, Eckhardt said at a Tribune event.

rows.title: Coronavirus throws Texas Supreme Court justices into the spotlight — and into Democrats’ crosshairs
rows.standfirst: In a year when four justices face reelection, the all-Republican high court has made a slate of controversy-generating decisions, including lifting a moratorium on evictions and — for now — limiting voting by mail in this year’s elections.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott instructs state agencies to trim budgets by 5% to prepare for “economic shock”
rows.standfirst: Some state agencies are exempt from the cuts, including the Department of State Health Services, the Texas Workforce Commission and the Department of Public Safety.

rows.title: TribCast: Bars are back, but questions remain on child care and voting by mail in a pandemic
rows.standfirst: In this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Aliyya and Ross about the latest reopenings in Texas amid missed benchmarks, child care complications for low-income parents and swirling voting-by-mail questions.

rows.title: Federal appeals court temporarily blocks voting-by-mail expansion in Texas
rows.standfirst: While a panel of the U.S. 5th Circuit Court of Appeals put one federal judge’s ruling on hold, the Texas Supreme Court heard arguments Wednesday in a separate case aimed at limiting mail-in voting.

rows.title: UT-Austin will resume classes this fall — but students won’t return to campus after Thanksgiving
rows.standfirst: After the November holiday, students will not return to campus in an effort to avoid spreading the coronavirus.

rows.title: Texas doctors say their revenue has dropped by at least 50% since the pandemic, survey data shows
rows.standfirst: Pandemic-related financial strain has hit independent medical practices especially hard, the survey showed. Many physicians have resorted to taking pay cuts or working fewer hours.

rows.title: “There won’t be a goodbye party”: Hospital administrator prepares to retire during pandemic
rows.standfirst: A hospital administrator gets a special gift. A food pantry worker gets her coronavirus test results. A Midland family cancels its annual fishing trip. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Texas is locked in a battle over voting by mail. Here’s how to do it.
rows.standfirst: It’s unclear whether Texas will expand who is eligible for a mail-in ballot during the pandemic, as other states have. But the people who normally qualify to vote by mail can still do so in July.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Driver’s license offices to gradually reopen
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas businesses returning during coronavirus are unlikely to spur fast economic recovery
rows.standfirst: As workers and customers reemerge into a society still grappling with a spreading coronavirus, the power Gov. Greg Abbott and officials across the globe used to close businesses in the first place does not extend to reviving the economy.

rows.title: Senate confirms U.S. Rep. John Ratcliffe of Texas as director of national intelligence
rows.standfirst: The congressman from Heath will oversee 17 intelligence agencies. His appointment creates a vacancy in one of Texas’ most conservative districts.

rows.title: Texas will test all residents and staff in state-run homes for people with disabilities
rows.standfirst: The test kits for residents of state supported living centers have been ordered and are on their way. The agency is “working on a broader plan to get the test kits for staff,” a state official said.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott lifts coronavirus restrictions for travelers from New York, Georgia and other hot spots
rows.standfirst: Travelers coming to Texas from select major states and cities previously had to undergo a mandatory 14-day self-quarantine.

rows.title: Federal cash infusion will start reaching Texas school districts in June
rows.standfirst: Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath told local school officials Thursday they can expect $1.29 billion in federal coronavirus relief to start flowing this summer, helping shore up district budgets for next school year.

rows.title: Texas families filing for SNAP food assistance almost doubled in April
rows.standfirst: Texas received a staggering 417,468 applications for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program last month, a sharp increase from March’s already high number of requests.

rows.title: After blowback, Texas admits 6% of its reported tests were for antibodies, not active infections
rows.standfirst: The state is now distinguishing antibody tests from standard viral tests.

rows.title: Analysis: Politics and a pandemic jumble Texas elections
rows.standfirst: The partisan differences about voting by mail in Texas — Democrats want to expand it, Republicans believe it’s insecure — were in place long before COVID-19 came along. But the pandemic has escalated the debate.

rows.title: They lost their jobs and insurance in the pandemic. Now they’re slipping through Texas’ health care safety net.
rows.standfirst: Texas had the highest uninsured rate of any state before the outbreak. It’s also among a minority of states that have declined to expand Medicaid coverage to people with incomes near or below the poverty line.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Bars, bowling alleys and other businesses can begin reopening Friday
rows.standfirst: Live updates: The state’s unemployment rate hit 12.8%, and a lawsuit seeks the release of medically vulnerable inmates in the Dallas County jail.

rows.title: For some, forgoing masks in public during the coronavirus pandemic has become a political statement
rows.standfirst: Mask arguments among Texans are occurring everywhere from retail stores to the highest levels of government.

rows.title: As Texas’ unemployment rate hits record high 12.8%, experts say the ongoing public health crisis will hamper an economic rebound
rows.standfirst: Until now, the state’s worst-ever monthly unemployment rate was 9.2% in November 1986, as Texas reeled from the last big oil bust. A combination of the coronavirus pandemic and a contracting energy industry are expected to slow Texas’ economic recovery.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says Texas is aiming to start college football on time, with fans in stands
rows.standfirst: The state is still working out a few issues, Abbott said Friday, but he predicted the season will return as scheduled, with at least some fans allowed to attend.

rows.title: After an “anticlimactic” virtual goodbye, Dell Medical School’s inaugural class heads to the front lines of the pandemic
rows.standfirst: On Thursday evening, Dell Medical School’s first cohort of students graduated in a virtual ceremony. Over the next month, the inaugural class will scatter across the country to begin residencies in the thick of a pandemic.

rows.title: “This is a scam”: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick calls it laughable for people under 65 to fear voting in person
rows.standfirst: Texas is locked in a legal battle over whether it must expand voting by mail.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Pence names Texas as a possible alternative GOP convention site
rows.standfirst: Live updates: Texas reports 55,971 cases and 1,527 deaths.

rows.title: As day cares reopen, a Texas parent weighs the risks of sending her kids back
rows.standfirst: Latonya Stott is excited to return to work full time, but she wants to wait a couple of weeks before sending her two youngest children to day care again. She explains why in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: Coronavirus hot spots in Texas homeless shelters highlight challenges unsheltered residents face social distancing, staying clean
rows.standfirst: Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner said officials there are spreading out homeless shelter residents after dozens tested positive in one day.

rows.title: Photos of Texas’ continued reopening: Bars, bowling alleys and other businesses welcome back customers
rows.standfirst: As Texas gradually reopens, bars were allowed to open their doors to start off Memorial Day weekend. Texas Tribune photographers were out Friday and Saturday to capture how that went in Austin.

rows.title: Influential conservative group endorses Ronny Jackson over Josh Winegarner in runoff for U.S. Rep. Mac Thornberry’s seat
rows.standfirst: The two men vying to represent the Texas Panhandle in Congress have split a slew of endorsements ahead of the runoff to replace Thornberry, who is retiring.

rows.title: Living in hotels, students lose ground while dealing with cramped rooms and eviction fears
rows.standfirst: Long-stay hotels are often the last resort for struggling families, even more so during the coronavirus pandemic. Many children are receiving little education with schools closed, and school districts have simply lost track of thousands of students.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: More than 26,000 workers in Texas’ oil and gas industry lost jobs in April
rows.standfirst: Live updates: The oilfield service sector accounted for more than 22,000 of the industry’s jobs lost in April, according to the Texas Workforce Commission.

rows.title: Water parks, food court dining areas added to Texas’ latest wave of reopenings
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott issued a proclamation Tuesday adding a few types of businesses to the list.

rows.title: Texas recommends people bring their own hand sanitizer to vote this summer
rows.standfirst: The secretary of state suggested that voters “may want to consider” voting curbside if they have symptoms of COVID-19, including a fever, cough or sore throat, when they arrive at a polling place.

rows.title: Analysis: Rising property values — and taxes — during an economic slump
rows.standfirst: Many Texas property owners are sweating potential increases in their taxes, which are based on property values that don’t reflect a pandemic, an oil price collapse or a slumping economy.

rows.title: Some Texas hospitals continued to sue patients for unpaid medical bills during the coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of debt collection lawsuits have been filed since Gov. Greg Abbott declared a state of disaster because of COVID-19 in mid-March, according to the Health Care Research and Policy Team at Johns Hopkins University.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: 250,000 Texans with approved unemployment claims have yet to request payment
rows.standfirst: Live updates: To receive benefits, people who filed for unemployment must request payments every two weeks on an assigned day.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says Amarillo has “turned a corner” after coronavirus flare-up
rows.standfirst: The Texas Panhandle, where a workforce of Hispanics and immigrants powers several meatpacking plants, is home to the highest rates of infection in the state.

rows.title: TribCast: How to vote in a pandemic and Texas’ record unemployment rate
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Emma and Ross about the state’s recently released guidance for the upcoming elections, the reopening of water parks and the economic devastation faced by Texas workers.

rows.title: Some Texans in Congress vote through proxies for the first time in American history
rows.standfirst: Republicans have fought the allowance of proxy voting tooth and nail. They argue that such a move upends the Constitution, and they promise a protracted legal fight.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court: Lack of immunity to coronavirus alone isn’t enough for mail-in ballot
rows.standfirst: Although the court sided with state Attorney General Ken Paxton’s interpretation of what constitutes a disability, it indicated that it is up to voters to assess their health and determine if they meet the state’s definition, which could allow them to vote by mail.

rows.title: Texas on the hook for $6.8 million after long voter ID fight
rows.standfirst: The state plans to appeal the Wednesday ruling from a federal judge in Corpus Christi.

rows.title: Former U.S. Rep. Sam Johnson, a Vietnam War veteran, has died
rows.standfirst: Johnson, R-Richardson, was first elected to Congress in 1991 and gained a reputation as a strong conservative voice in the Texas delegation. He was a prisoner of war for nearly seven years.

rows.title: The Castros say they’ll work to beat Donald Trump, but they haven’t made their support for Joe Biden official yet
rows.standfirst: The former presidential candidate and the U.S. representative from San Antonio, two of Texas’ most prominent Democrats, have yet to formally endorse the Democratic nominee for president.

rows.title: With a baby on the way, Midland couple has to decline in-person family celebrations
rows.standfirst: A family plans a drive-by baby shower. A Houston restaurant gears up to reopen its dining room. And an East Texas town regains a sense of normalcy. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: With three generations under one roof, pandemic risks multiply
rows.standfirst: The Golinelli family is among many Texas households navigating working in a pandemic while trying to keep high-risk older relatives safe from the coronavirus.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: State attributes new single-day record for positive cases to holiday weekend lag, increased testing in prisons
rows.standfirst: Live updates: About 2.2 million Texans have filed for unemployment during the pandemic. Gov. Greg Abbott allows spectators for pro sports.

rows.title: House Democrats demand Trump administration stop rushing through deportations of migrant children
rows.standfirst: Democratic congressional leaders expressed alarm at the sudden acceleration and requested the government “cease this practice immediately.”

rows.title: Did your child get free or reduced-price school lunches? You may be eligible for $285 in food aid.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission on Monday extended the deadline for applying to July 31.

rows.title: Community colleges trying to help students who are losing jobs, child care
rows.standfirst: For Texas community college students, the pandemic upended delicate balances of work, family and financial survival. Schools are tapping into emergency funds and trying to connect students with needed services.

rows.title: Joe Biden to address Texas Democratic Party convention June 6
rows.standfirst: The presumptive presidential nominee will close out the party’s virtual convention.

rows.title: Texas sports fans will soon be allowed to attend outdoor pro games, Gov. Greg Abbott says
rows.standfirst: Starting Friday, most Texas counties will be able to host in-person spectators for outdoor sporting events in venues. But occupancy will be limited to 25%.

rows.title: House approves bill spearheaded by U.S. Rep. Chip Roy to ease restrictions on small-business loan program
rows.standfirst: The freshman representative from Texas teamed up with a Democrat from Minnesota to pass the bill, which will now head to the U.S. Senate.

rows.title: As Texas inmates’ lawsuit over coronavirus response winds through courts, infections among prisoners surge
rows.standfirst: Judges questioned both the inmates’ arguments and state’s positions in a Thursday hearing. In April, the appeals court temporarily blocked a lower judge’s order against the Texas Department of Criminal Justice over its coronavirus practices and policies at a geriatric prison.

rows.title: Texas Southern University gave $2 million in aid to unqualified students, review finds
rows.standfirst: A new review sheds more light on an admissions scandal that has plagued the Houston school since November and led to the ouster of former President Austin Lane.

rows.title: Texas will extend early voting period this fall, Gov. Greg Abbott says
rows.standfirst: Abbott has already added more time to the early voting period for the July runoff election, citing the need to create a safe environment for in-person voting during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Analysis: Judges deal Texans more confusion about voting by mail
rows.standfirst: If you were looking for voting-by-mail advice from the Texas Supreme Court, you’re out of luck. The court ruled that the pandemic is no reason to expand voting by mail, but also that election officials don’t have to check voter claims of disability.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Texas A&M System approves a plan for in-person classes during pandemic
rows.standfirst: Live updates: Texas reported 1,230 new coronavirus cases Friday. At least 61,006 Texans have tested positive for the virus, and 1,626 have died.

rows.title: Texas A&M System makes plans for how to handle in-person instruction this fall
rows.standfirst: Texas A&M University System officials voted Friday on systemwide guidance for the fall semester. While some face-to-face classes will resume, many will be conducted in a hybrid model, using a combination of online and in-person instruction.

rows.title: Texas elected leaders condemn the death of George Floyd as “horrific,” “senseless”
rows.standfirst: In a TV interview Friday, Gov. Greg Abbott said said that the death of Floyd, a black man who was killed Monday in Minneapolis police custody, “should not have happened.” But Texas’ GOP congressional officials declined to comment on President Donald Trump’s “looting” tweet.

rows.title: Is El Paso ready to reopen? Not all Texas officials agree.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott gave El Paso an extra week to implement the latest phase of reopening. The county judge says El Paso still isn’t ready to take the next step, but the governor isn’t giving the city an extension.

rows.title: Three top Texas GOP officials who oppose expanding mail-in voting have each used it
rows.standfirst: Texas’ top Republican officials call absentee voting a recipe for fraud and are fighting efforts to expand it during the coronavirus pandemic. But the governor, lieutenant governor and attorney general have all used the option.

rows.title: President Donald Trump to visit Dallas as he resumes in-person campaign fundraisers
rows.standfirst: The president is set to attend a high-dollar fundraiser June 11 in the North Texas city.

rows.title: As Texans demonstrate anger over George Floyd’s death, Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner asks for “peaceful” protests
rows.standfirst: Floyd, a black man who formerly lived in Houston, was killed in Minneapolis police custody after a white officer kneeled on his neck. Hundreds in Houston turned out Friday to demonstrate their anger over his death.

rows.title: GOP voter registration group shutters amid coronavirus challenges
rows.standfirst: The super PAC Engage Texas raised nearly $13 million and hired hundreds of staffers but was not able to see a path forward as the pandemic persisted.

rows.title: A weekend of protest and mourning: George Floyd’s death spurs demonstrations in Texas cities
rows.standfirst: Floyd, who was raised in Houston’s Third Ward, was killed in Minneapolis by police. Officer Derek Chauvin has been fired, and charged with third-degree murder and manslaughter. Rallies and protests are happening all over the nation, including in several Texas cities.

rows.title: San Antonio mayor imposes curfew to curb protesting
rows.standfirst: After a demonstration against police violence blocked traffic in Austin on Interstate 35, police used tear gas and rubber bullets.

rows.title: She worries voting in person could put her grandmother at risk of contracting coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Sara Sullivan wishes every Texan who wanted a mail-in ballot could get one, especially during the pandemic. Listen to her story in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: Dallas, San Antonio extend curfews through Sunday night
rows.standfirst: Throughout the weekend, protesters marched in Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio and Fort Worth, clashing with police officers, over the death of George Floyd.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott declares state of disaster after George Floyd protests
rows.standfirst: In a statement, Abbott said the declaration would allow him to designate federal agents to serve as peace officers in Texas.
